question: Does the parameter-slot-count tie-break generalize safely to multi-slot mechanisms (2 vs 1 slot), template-only params with parameter_slots=[] but template ${id}, and equal-slot-count ties (0 vs 0 or 1 vs 1)?
hypothesis: The parameter-slot-count tie-break (Option A from EXP-GRAPH-33816735314) generalizes safely: (1) a 2-slot mechanism wins over a 1-slot mechanism at equal confidence because len(parameter_slots)=2 > 1; (2) a template-only param mechanism (parameter_slots=[] but template contains ${id}) loses to a 1-slot param mechanism at equal confidence because len(parameter_slots)=0 < 1; (3) equal-slot-count ties (0 vs 0, 1 vs 1) remain degenerate (ID-dependent, not deterministic by slot count); (4) no existing mechanism type regresses. The tie-break does not introduce regressions for cold, literal-only, or param-only baselines.
falsifier: The hypothesis is FALSIFIED if ANY of: (1) COMPETE_2VS1_EQUAL returns the 1-slot mechanism instead of the 2-slot mechanism — multi-slot tie-break fails; (2) COMPETE_TEMPLATE_VS_PARAM returns the template-only param mechanism instead of the 1-slot param — template-only param not correctly subordinated; (3) Any baseline condition (B_COLD, B_LITERAL, B_PARAM_1SLOT, B_PARAM_2SLOT) produces a different result than specified — regression; (4) Positive or null control fails — confidence dominance broken; (5) Code fix causes Python exceptions, type errors, or unexpected resolution statuses in any condition.
baselines: B_COLD: Register no mechanisms. Resolve with params={id: 2}. Expected: UNKNOWN. Replicates parent cold-null validation.

B_LITERAL: Register ONLY literal mechanism (parameter_slots=[], action_template={url: /posts/1}). Resolve with params={id: 1}. Expected: EXECUTABLE, bound_action url=/posts/1. Verifies literal standalone unchanged.

B_PARAM_1SLOT: Register ONLY 1-slot param mechanism (parameter_slots=['id'], action_template={url: /posts/${id}}). Resolve with params={id: 1}. Expected: EXECUTABLE, bound_action url=/posts/1. Verifies 1-slot param standalone unchanged.

B_PARAM_2SLOT: Register ONLY 2-slot param mechanism (parameter_slots=['user_id', 'post_id'], action_template={url: /users/${user_id}/posts/${post_id}}). Resolve with params={user_id: 1, post_id: 1}. Expected: EXECUTABLE, bound_action url=/users/1/posts/1. Verifies 2-slot param standalone works.
positive_control: Register 2-slot param with higher confidence (0.98) than 1-slot param (0.95) in shared registry. Resolve with params={user_id: 1, post_id: 1, id: 1}. Must return EXECUTABLE with 2-slot mechanism winning by confidence (not tie-break). Verifies confidence dominance works for multi-slot mechanisms.
null_control: Register 1-slot param with higher confidence (0.98) than 2-slot param (0.95) in shared registry. Resolve with params={user_id: 1, post_id: 1, id: 1}. Must return EXECUTABLE with 1-slot mechanism winning by confidence. Verifies confidence dominance works in reverse for multi-slot mechanisms.
measurement_validity: All conditions use identical kernel logic and mechanism definitions as parent experiment EXP-GRAPH-33816735314, maintaining substrate continuity.
No HTTP execution required — only resolution and bound_action correctness measured. Eliminates network variability.
Each condition uses a fresh kernel instance with explicitly controlled registry contents. No cross-contamination.
The code fix is the same single-line change as the parent experiment: candidates.sort(key=lambda m: (m.confidence, len(m.parameter_slots)), reverse=True) applied in the test script.
All conditions deterministic: no model calls, no RNG, no sampling.
Multi-slot, template-only, and equal-slot-count conditions are NEW measurements not present in the parent experiment. They test the tie-break's boundary conditions.
Pre-fix baseline replication conditions are exact replications of parent conditions to verify no regression.

conditions.description: Template-only param vs 1-slot param at equal confidence (0.95)
conditions.note: 1-slot wins: len(parameter_slots)=1 > 0 (template-only has parameter_slots=[] even though template has ${id})

conditions.description: Template-only param vs literal at equal confidence (0.95)
conditions.note: Both have len(parameter_slots)=0; tie-break is degenerate, winner depends on insertion order. This is an expected limitation.

conditions.description: Two 1-slot params (different templates) at equal confidence (0.95)
conditions.note: Both have len(parameter_slots)=1; tie-break is degenerate, winner depends on insertion order.

conditions.description: Two literals (different URLs) at equal confidence (0.95)
conditions.note: Both have len(parameter_slots)=0; tie-break is degenerate, winner depends on insertion order.

decision_rule: MULTI-SLOT-SAFE if ALL of: (1) B_COLD → UNKNOWN; (2) B_LITERAL → EXECUTABLE url=/posts/1; (3) B_PARAM_1SLOT → EXECUTABLE url=/posts/1; (4) B_PARAM_2SLOT → EXECUTABLE url=/users/1/posts/1; (5) COMPETE_2VS1_EQUAL → EXECUTABLE with 2-slot mechanism as winner; (6) COMPETE_TEMPLATE_VS_PARAM → EXECUTABLE with 1-slot mechanism as winner; (7) POS_CONTROL → EXECUTABLE with 2-slot mechanism as winner; (8) NULL_CONTROL → EXECUTABLE with 1-slot mechanism as winner. MULTI-SLOT-UNSAFE if any baseline condition regresses OR COMPETE_2VS1_EQUAL returns 1-slot OR COMPETE_TEMPLATE_VS_PARAM returns template-only param. DEGENERATE if conditions COMPETE_TEMPLATE_VS_LITERAL, COMPETE_1VS1_EQUAL, COMPETE_0VS0_EQUAL show ID-dependent behavior (expected, recorded but not gate-failing). MEASUREMENT_INVALID if code fix causes exceptions or unexpected resolution statuses.
product_consequence_positive: If MULTI-SLOT-SAFE: the parameter-slot-count tie-break generalizes to multi-slot mechanisms. C-PARAM-INHERIT advances further. Product registration of multi-slot mechanisms becomes safe at equal confidence. The kernel can handle mechanisms with arbitrary slot counts. Template-only params are correctly subordinated to declared-slot params.
product_consequence_negative: If MULTI-SLOT-UNSAFE: the tie-break does not generalize to multi-slot mechanisms. The 'required_slots vs parameter_slots divergence' issue (template-only params declare no slots but require params) needs to be addressed. C-PARAM-INHERIT remains limited to single-slot mechanisms. The kernel may need a different tie-break strategy (e.g., tie-breaking on len(required_slots) instead of len(parameter_slots)).
estimated_cost: Negligible — pure kernel resolution logic, no HTTP execution, no model calls. 11 conditions, each a fresh kernel instance. The code fix is a single-line change applied in the test script. Execution time < 5 seconds.
expected_information_gain: HIGH for C-PARAM-INHERIT. This directly tests whether the tie-break generalizes to multi-slot and template-only mechanisms — the primary unknown from EXP-GRAPH-33816735314. Both outcomes advance the decision: SAFE extends the fix's applicability to multi-slot mechanisms; UNSAFE identifies the template-only param divergence issue and narrows the search to alternative tie-break strategies. The degenerate equal-slot-count conditions expose known limitations without blocking the gate.
